neighbours.label: What becomes of an abolished or closed body's functions, staff or assets (handover after dissolution: 'were abolished, and most of their functions transferred'), vs the same organisations described without a dissolution
fire: The board was dissolved in 1974, and most of its duties passed to the county council.
When the ministry was abolished, its remaining staff moved to the treasury.
The old trust was wound up and all of its assets went to the city.
After the agency closed, most of its powers were handed to regional offices.
The college was merged out of existence, and its library went to the university.
The commission was scrapped in 2010 and its tasks were shared among three departments.
Once the parish council was abolished, its records were sent to the county archive.
The bank was liquidated, and most of its clients were moved to a rival.
quiet: The board was enlarged in 1974, and most of its duties stayed the same.
When the ministry was renamed, its staff kept working in the same building.
The old trust held a meeting and all of its members voted.
After the agency opened, most of its offices were busy all day.
The college grew quickly, and its library bought many new books.
The commission met in 2010 and its members discussed three reports.
Once the parish council was elected, its members met every month.
The bank was profitable, and most of its clients were happy.

predictions: Post-abolition clauses about functions or staff reach 0.4-0.8; the same bodies described as continuing or growing stay under 0.15.
notes: Card: their functions transferred to the City, transfer of the fire engine, migrate content, reassigned users. Probe: 'abolished, and most of their functions transferred' 0.821, 'abolished, and most of their staff retired' 0.515 (on staff), migrate contents 0.253, transfer of 0.132, reassigned 0.110; repair of the fire engine 0.007.
